questions.q: Where do column descriptions and data tests live in a dbt project, according to this lesson?
options: In the exact same YAML file, on the exact same column, in the same block
Descriptions live in a separate wiki, tests live only in .sql files
Descriptions live in dbt_project.yml, tests live in schema.yml
Neither can be defined in YAML — both require custom macros
questions.explain: dbt Labs' own example shows event_id carrying both a description: and its data_tests: together in one block, which is the whole point of this pairing.

questions.q: What is the practical difference between a folded block (`>`) and a literal block (`|`) description in YAML?
options: `>` collapses interior line breaks into one paragraph; `|` preserves them, useful for structured content like lists
`>` is for models only; `|` is for columns only
`|` disables Markdown rendering; `>` enables it
They are functionally identical with no difference in output
questions.explain: Folded block (>) is the default for normal prose; literal block (|) keeps line breaks when the description itself needs internal structure.

questions.q: What happens to a column that has no description written for it?
options: It still appears in the generated docs site with whatever metadata dbt can introspect from the warehouse, just without a human-written description
dbt refuses to compile the project until every column is documented
The column is silently dropped from the model
A generic, auto-generated description is inserted automatically
questions.explain: Documentation isn't all-or-nothing — undocumented columns still show real metadata like name and type, just no human-written explanation.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what's the honest approach to deciding which columns to document?
options: Document columns whose meaning genuinely isn't obvious, and skip writing a description that just restates an already-clear column name
Every single column must always have a full paragraph description
Only primary key columns should ever be documented
Descriptions should be written by an AI tool automatically for every column
questions.explain: Writing 'the customer ID' for a column already named customer_id adds documentation debt without adding real information.

questions.q: Why does keeping descriptions and tests in the same YAML block matter more than convenience, according to this lesson?
options: Splitting them into separate systems (a wiki vs. a test file) means nothing forces them to be updated together, so they drift apart over time
YAML files run faster when descriptions and tests are combined
dbt requires descriptions and tests to be in the same file or it throws a compile error
It has no real benefit beyond saving a few lines of code
questions.explain: Co-locating them makes it likely a change to one gets noticed alongside the other — the real problem this pairing solves is drift, not just convenience.
